symptom: Static catalog audit found that the v347 contract test accepted a nonempty replacement of a case's mutation or independentFixtureState while preserving its case ID, lane, denial and false authorization flags. Thus a future verifier harness could execute a different negative scenario under the original case ID without the catalog guard detecting semantic drift. No verifier, independent evidence or scoring path was executed.
lesson: A deny-only fixture catalog is not frozen by case IDs and expected denial codes alone. A changed mutation or independently provisioned fixture precondition can silently redefine what a future verifier test is supposed to falsify while preserving its apparent PASS classification.
guardrail: Pin each negative case's semantic mutation and independent fixture precondition alongside its expected first denial and lane. Exercise deliberate mutation/state drift in contract regression tests, and preserve explicit untrusted request/response contract identities. Treat static catalog checks as specification integrity only, never independent verification.
